title: Miu Hirano and Ryoichi Yoshiyama knock out China's last singles players at WTT Contender Istanbul
seo_title: WTT Contender Istanbul: Hirano and Yoshiyama in semis
description: Miu Hirano beat Zong Geman and Ryoichi Yoshiyama beat Li Tianyang in the WTT Contender Istanbul quarter-finals, leaving China with nobody in any final.
standfirst: Three Japanese women reach the last four, while all four men's semi-finalists are unseeded after Kang Dongsoo beat the third seed without dropping a game.
body: Miu Hirano and Ryoichi Yoshiyama beat the last two Chinese singles players at WTT Contender Istanbul on Saturday morning, which means China will have nobody in any of the tournament's five finals.

Hirano, the world No 25, came through a deciding game against 20-year-old Zong Geman 6-11, 11-3, 11-8, 7-11, 11-8, and Yoshiyama, 22, came from two games down to beat China's 19-year-old fifth seed, Li Tianyang, 12-14, 8-11, 11-9, 11-7, 11-6.
## Hirano wins a second decider in two days

It was Hirano's first meeting with Zong, and the second day running that she had needed five games, after her [comeback against Croatia's Hana Arapovic](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-connor-green-anna-hursey-mixed-semi-finals-poret-nagasaki.html) in the last 16. Zong, ranked 76th, had already knocked out the third seed, Miyu Nagasaki, and won the first game comfortably. Hirano took the next two, lost the fourth 11-7, and from 7-7 in the decider won three points in a row to reach match point.

China's other women had gone out earlier in the week, including Qin Yuxuan, the sixth seed, beaten by Japan's Saki Shibata in the last 16. Their doubles pairs were also beaten: Qin and Zong in the women's quarter-finals, and Huang Youzheng and Qin in the mixed doubles semi-finals on Friday.
## Three Japanese women in the last four

Hirano now plays her compatriot Honoka Hashimoto, the top seed and world No 14, who lost only 13 points against Brazil's Bruna Takahashi, the eighth seed, winning 11-3, 11-4, 11-6. The two will meet again on Sunday in the women's doubles final, Hashimoto with Miyu Nagasaki and Hirano with Miyuu Kihara.

The other semi-final is between Japan's Kaho Akae and South Korea's Joo Cheonhui, the second seed. Akae, 22 and ranked 37th, won an all-Japanese quarter-final against Shibata 12-10, 11-8, 11-9, and Joo, the world No 17, beat Romania's Bernadette Szőcs, the fifth seed, 11-7, 11-9, 11-5.
## No seeds left in the men's draw

Three men's seeds reached the quarter-finals and all three lost. Sweden's Elias Ranefur, the third seed and world No 27, went out to South Korea's Kang Dongsoo in a match in which every game went beyond 10-10. Kang, 32 and ranked 120th, won all three, 14-12, 12-10, 13-11, a day after beating Russia's Nikita Artemenko in five games.

Yoshiyama, the world No 62, had beaten the second seed, France's Thibault Poret, on Friday. Against Li, ranked 42nd, he lost a first game that went to 14-12 and then the second 11-8, before taking the last three 11-9, 11-7, 11-6.

So all four men's semi-finalists are unseeded. Kang plays Yoshiyama, and the other semi-final is between two 34-year-olds. Germany's Ricardo Walther, ranked 143rd, ended the run of Norway's Borgar Haug, the qualifier who [beat Quadri Aruna](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-qualifying-ends-quadri-aruna-borgar-haug-main-draw.html), 11-9, 13-11, 6-11, 11-6. Kazakhstan's Fang Bo, the runner-up at the 2015 World Championships and now back on the tour after years away from China's national team, beat the Czech seventh seed Lubomir Jancarik 11-4, 11-4, 11-9.

- Women's singles: Honoka Hashimoto (JPN) bt Bruna Takahashi (BRA) 11-3, 11-4, 11-6; Miu Hirano (JPN) bt Zong Geman (CHN) 6-11, 11-3, 11-8, 7-11, 11-8; Kaho Akae (JPN) bt Saki Shibata (JPN) 12-10, 11-8, 11-9; Joo Cheonhui (KOR) bt Bernadette Szőcs (ROU) 11-7, 11-9, 11-5
- Men's singles: Ricardo Walther (GER) bt Borgar Haug (NOR) 11-9, 13-11, 6-11, 11-6; Fang Bo (KAZ) bt Lubomir Jancarik (CZE) 11-4, 11-4, 11-9; Kang Dongsoo (KOR) bt Elias Ranefur (SWE) 14-12, 12-10, 13-11; Ryoichi Yoshiyama (JPN) bt Li Tianyang (CHN) 12-14, 8-11, 11-9, 11-7, 11-6

The singles semi-finals are this afternoon, followed by the first final of the week, with England's Connor Green and Wales's Anna Hursey [playing Russia's Evgeny Tikhonov and Maria Panfilova](/news/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026-connor-green-anna-hursey-mixed-doubles-final.html) for the mixed doubles title.

- 1.30pm UK: Honoka Hashimoto v Miu Hirano, women's singles
- 2.05pm: Ricardo Walther v Fang Bo, men's singles
- 2.40pm: Kaho Akae v Joo Cheonhui, women's singles
- 3.15pm: Kang Dongsoo v Ryoichi Yoshiyama, men's singles
- 3.50pm: Connor Green / Anna Hursey v Evgeny Tikhonov / Maria Panfilova, mixed doubles final

Times are approximate. The women's and men's doubles finals start at about 11am UK time on Sunday, before the singles finals. Every match is on WTT's YouTube channel, with live scores on Eleven's [event page](/events/wtt-contender-istanbul-2026.html#matches).
